english.title: Owner / master / person responsible for conduct of vessel contravene the Merchant Shipping regulations
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) **(..SPECIFY DETAILS OF THE OFFENCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 6 of the Merchant Shipping (Distress Signals and Prevention of Collisions) Regulations 1996.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Regulation 6(2) of the Merchant Shipping (Distress Signals and Prevention of Collisions) Regulations 1996 provides a defence.
(ii) Regulation 7 contains a power to detain a ship.
(iii) This regulation applies to watercraft as it applies to ships with the modification set out in Schedule 2 to the Merchant Shipping (Watercraft) Order 2023.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Note:
The summary penalty is different for an infringement of Rule 10(b)(i) (duty to proceed with traffic flow in lanes of separation schemes) of the International Regulations as defined in Regulation 1(3).On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
